definitions: A class of broad-spectrum antibiotics, including penicillin, that contain a beta-lactam ring in their molecular structure and act by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis.
Any antibiotic characterized by a beta-lactam ring, effective against a wide range of bacteria.
examples: Penicillin is a well-known beta-lactam antibiotic.
The doctor prescribed a beta-lactam antibiotic for the infection.
Resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics is a growing concern.
